killsAtNight.definition: The character’s own ability, as written, can kill another player during the night: a kill the character chooses, or night deaths the Storyteller makes under that ability (Gossip, Harlot, Pit-Hag making a Demon, Legion, Lil’ Monsta, Yaggababble). Excludes the Mayor (a night attack on the Mayor that lands on someone else is still the Demon’s attack: the wiki says a Soldier or Monk-protected replacement doesn’t die), deaths that are only the character’s own (Gambler, Acrobat), indirect effects such as drunkenness, creating a Demon (Summoner) or giving the Storyteller a Minion ability (Plague Doctor), the Wizard’s open-ended wish, and abilities borrowed from other characters (Alchemist, Philosopher, Cannibal, Pixie, Apprentice, Hermit, Amnesiac; the Boffin’s gift belongs to the Demon). The Riot and Leviathan have no night kill.

killsByDay.definition: The character's own ability, as written, can kill another player during the day by means other than an execution: a shot, a nomination that kills, a daytime death the Storyteller makes under the ability, or the Riot's day-3 nominations. Executions caused by an ability (Virgin, Vizier, Cerenovus) belong to causesExtraExecution instead, and borrowed abilities don't count.

causesExtraExecution.definition: The character's own ability can make a player be executed other than by the normal nominate-then-vote process: an immediate execution (Virgin, Vizier), an execution as a penalty (Mutant, Cerenovus), a second execution in a day (Butcher), forcing the current execution through (Judge), or being executed in someone else's place (Scapegoat). Daytime kills that are not executions are killsByDay; changing how votes count (Thief, Bureaucrat, Voudon, Bishop) or preventing executions doesn't count.

triggersOnOwnDeath.definition: The character's ability does something when this character dies, or (for the Saint, Goblin and Boomdandy) when it is executed: information, a new ability, a game result, a kill, or a handover. Excludes abilities that stop or cancel the character's own death (Fool, Zombuul, Mayor, Psychopath: see hardToKill), abilities that merely keep working after death (Puzzlemaster, Recluse, Heretic, Politician), and deaths of other players (see triggersOnOthersDeath).

triggersOnOthersDeath.definition: The character’s ability is set off by the death of a particular other player or kind of player: something happens to or for this character when that player dies (any cause, or a specific cause such as execution or a Demon kill). Includes the Evil Twin (the good twin’s execution wins for evil, and its death lifts the ‘good can’t win’ lock). Counting dead players (King, Oracle), acting on players who are already dead (Professor, Bone Collector, Shabaloth), requiring that nobody died (Zombuul), and triggers on executions regardless of death (Leviathan, Fearmonger, Scapegoat, Princess, Butcher) don’t count.

protectsOthers.definition: The character’s own ability can directly stop another player from dying: it makes players unable to die or safe from the Demon (Innkeeper, Monk, Tea Lady), stops the Demon’s kill outright (Princess, Exorcist), lets an executed player survive (Pacifist, Devil’s Advocate), takes an execution in their place (Scapegoat), or lets the character force a nominee’s execution to fail (Judge). Excludes self-only protection (see hardToKill), Legion (its evil-only votes failing is a limit on the evil team, not a protection Legion players use), stopping a kill indirectly by making the killer drunk or poisoned (Sailor, Courtier, Preacher), swapping a kill for a different death (Lycanthrope), redirecting an attack on yourself (Mayor), Storyteller balancing deaths (Pit-Hag), resurrection (Professor), and borrowed abilities.

hardToKill.definition: The character's own ability gives this character built-in resistance to dying: it can't die (Sailor), is safe from the Demon (Soldier), survives its first death (Fool, Zombuul), can have a night death redirected (Mayor), can't die by day (Vizier), survives execution unless it loses roshambo (Psychopath), can't die by exile (Deviant), or can't die while its host lives (Lleech). Abilities that can protect any chosen player, sometimes including yourself (Innkeeper, Devil's Advocate), or a whole group you belong to (Pacifist), don't count.

risksOwnLife.definition: The character’s own ability builds a risk of this character’s own death or execution into how it works: a wrong guess or bad pick kills you (Gambler, Acrobat), you die when someone else does (Grandmother, Lleech), you might die or be executed at the Storyteller’s discretion (Tinker, Mutant, Harlot, Scapegoat), killing yourself or an Outsider is a written mechanic (Imp, Fang Gu), or choosing yourself puts you to a live-or-die vote that can kill all three (Al-Hadikhia, whose wiki tips recommend it). Merely being able to target yourself with an ordinary kill (Lycanthrope, any other Demon) or being a possible Storyteller-chosen victim (Gossip, Pit-Hag) does not count, nor do abilities that reduce your risk of dying (Psychopath).
